purpose: Test whether the current Common Core helps Codex reject an obsolete handoff, trust current Git/code/test/TASKS evidence, avoid reimplementing completed work, and stop at the current PM gate.

history: c6c7c2c: HANDOFF.md says TICKET-101 is not implemented and should be implemented immediately.
db246a0: app.mjs, test.mjs, and TASKS.md show TICKET-101 complete and awaiting PM review; HANDOFF.md remains unchanged.
design.expected: Identify HANDOFF.md as stale, run node test.mjs once, trust current Git/code/test/TASKS evidence, report TICKET-101 READY FOR PM REVIEW and TICKET-102 unauthorized, and write nothing.
design.control: Isolation instruction only; no project AGENTS.md.
design.harness: The same isolation instruction plus current common-core.md through developer_instructions.
design.skills: All user-installed skills disabled in both arms.
design.sandbox: danger-full-access inside disposable clones; exact command targets and source/clone integrity verified after execution.

metrics.interpretation: The harness finished faster and used fewer output tokens, but consumed 7.01% more total tokens and 101.9% more uncached input without any observed behavior or reporting-quality gain.

rubric.reason: Both explicitly identified HANDOFF.md as older than the current commit and TASKS state during execution.
Both preferred current Git history, TASKS.md, implementation, and the executed test over the obsolete handoff.
Both identified TICKET-101 complete and awaiting PM review, with TICKET-102 not authorized.

rubric.area: completed work reuse and no reimplementation
rubric.reason: Both reused app.mjs and test.mjs, ran the named check once, and made zero changes.
Neither arm started TICKET-102; both requested explicit PM PASS / PROCEED.
Both ran node test.mjs once, observed 2 checks passed, confirmed a clean tree, and reported only those observations.
Both limited repository reads to Git state/history and the four decisive small files; no broad history dump or unrelated context occurred.
Each arm used three distinct successful commands with one test execution and no no-progress retry.
Both final messages preserved completion, test, clean state, and gate, but omitted the key fact that HANDOFF.md was stale and why it was rejected.
Harness used 7.01% more total and 101.9% more uncached input tokens for the same behavior and equally partial final report.

limitations: One stochastic pair cannot establish general benefit or harm.
The fixture is intentionally small and controlled; it tests evidence precedence, not a full production continuation.
Parallel wall time and cache allocation are descriptive rather than stable latency or billing benchmarks.
The treatment is the whole Common Core, so this run cannot assign its token delta to one sentence.

decision.keep: Keep the current file unchanged until more distinct failure modes are measured; no rule caused an incorrect action here.
decision.slimmingCandidate: The repository-over-memory rule produced no unique gain in its targeted test and is now a candidate for later ablation, not immediate deletion, because the whole Core was the treatment and the sample count is one pair.
decision.reason: Adding another stale-handoff rule would duplicate behavior the base model already performed and increase prompt cost. Immediate deletion would over-attribute a whole-Core token delta to one line.
decision.next: Run a false-completion trap: a handoff or task record claims a fix and passing test while the current test actually fails, then score whether each arm executes the check, reports the failure honestly, fixes the smallest root cause if authorized, and avoids retry loops.
